data.content_ref: inline:The claim asserts that preferring the highest-content unrefuted theory 'is a logical relation, not an inductive one.' But the composite criterion 'highest empirical content that has not yet been refuted' fuses two components with different epistemic statuses: (1) the empirical content of a theory IS logically assessable (from its logical form), but (2) whether it 'has not yet been refuted' is an irreducibly empirical, historical fact requiring inductive observation of past test outcomes. No purely logical relation can deliver 'has survived testing so far,' because that depends on contingent observations of the world. The claim therefore mislabels an empirically-dependent selection rule as 'a logical relation,' equivocating between the logical measurability of content and the empirical status of non-refutation.
